findings.claim: In a sandboxed srcdoc frame, normalizing a locked activity fragment creates a Back loop. When replaceState throws, historyChanged() falls back to assigning location.hash to the current activity, which pushes a new history entry instead of replacing the locked one. Each later Back returns to the locked entry, which is normalized by pushing again, so Back can no longer move past that point in the frame (inferred, not tested: the host page Back button traverses the same joint session history and would hit the same loop). This predates d3715dcd (the same fallback existed at 2f281e85) and is not reachable from any page control: no in-page link produces an #activity-N fragment outside the guarded timeline and back links, so it needs a host- or devtools-driven fragment change inside the frame.

evidence.section: artifact.html line 1321, historyChanged() locked-fragment normalization and its location.hash fallback (textSha256 is of that exact source line). Observation: Reproduced on this page with Playwright 1.55 Chromium from the repository node_modules (no screenshots, no traces) in a sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc frame, where history.pushState and replaceState throw SecurityError: after reaching activity 3 through the committed public route, a locked #activity-4 fragment was normalized to #activity-2 but history.length grew by two; after Previous, seven Backs were pressed in total: the first showed activity 2, and each of the other six landed on the locked entry, was pushed forward again to #activity-2, and stayed on activity 2 with history.length fixed. Top-level (replaceState available) the same sequence walked back normally to activity 1. A probe showed location.replace with a fragment in this sandboxed srcdoc frame navigates the frame away and loses the page, so it is not a safe substitute.

findings.recommendation: When replaceState is unavailable, keep the current activity without rewriting the fragment (leave the locked fragment in place, as foreign fragments already are), or otherwise avoid adding an entry during normalization; keep the pushState-failure fallback in go() and Continue, which correctly adds an entry for real forward navigation. Note for the reconciler: leaving the locked fragment in place departs from the DESIGN.md sentence that a disallowed fragment normalizes, but in this sandbox normalization without adding an entry is not available (replaceState throws and location.replace reloads the frame), so the choice is between that sentence and a Back loop.

Loop-4 ruling on current bytes at d3715dcd (HEAD 1a645b15; sha256 e3de63fb53e42e04096263aeb25d9b79688075ecc33da7cd4a4fae551b2610f1). git diff 2f281e85 d3715dcd on this page changes exactly 11 lines, and the non-wording lines are byte-identical on all eight pages: one print rule, three lines carrying the reworded location sentences, and seven engine lines (go, restart, the Continue capture handler, the guard declaration, its comment, historyChanged, and the Objectives Escape handler). restart() (line 1288) now sets main data-pep-complete to false when it reads true, after deleting the restarted activity's done/settled/attempt state; show() still writes completion only on the recap, and a grep of data-pep-complete on all eight pages finds no other writer (the remaining matches are the per-section data-pep-completed hooks). Rule: DESIGN.md State model ("Because it clears that activity's credit, page completion is false until the activity passes again"; navigation never changes it). Verified with Playwright 1.55 Chromium from the repository node_modules (no screenshots, no traces) using the committed public success route from this topic's qa-paths.json, replayed at runtime (actions split at each Continue click so the activity-2 segment could be replayed after Restart; no route value is copied into this file), in eight runs: top-level file:// and a sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc frame, each with pointer Restart and keyboard Restart (focus plus Enter). In every run: the route reached the recap with completion true and four of four credits; timeline navigation to activity 2 left completion true; Restart set it false, zeroed only activity 2 credit (credits 1,0,1,1; progress 3 of 4 done); timeline navigation after Restart kept it false; replaying the activity-2 segment re-passed it (four of four, completion still false while off the recap, which matches the attribute only ever being set on the recap at first completion too); Continue to the recap set it true again. No page errors. Resolved.

Loop-4 ruling on current bytes at d3715dcd (HEAD 1a645b15; sha256 e3de63fb53e42e04096263aeb25d9b79688075ecc33da7cd4a4fae551b2610f1). historyChanged() (line 1321) now returns early for any non-empty fragment that is not #activity-N, so a foreign fragment keeps the current activity (no state change), an empty fragment still means activity 1, and a locked #activity-N fragment is rewritten to the current one. The guard is now a string holding the expected target fragment, set only around the location.hash fallback and cleared by the first popstate or hashchange whose hash equals it, so it suppresses exactly the event the page caused and cannot go stale (it is cleared again if the setter throws). Verified with Playwright 1.55 Chromium from the repository node_modules (no screenshots, no traces), reaching activities 2 and 3 only through the committed public route segments. Top-level (pushState path) and sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc (pushState and replaceState throw SecurityError there, so the location.hash fallback runs): Continue, Continue, Back, Forward, Back each showed the activity named by the fragment with no swallowed traversal; a foreign fragment on activity 2 kept activity 2, left state unchanged and stayed in the URL; a locked #activity-4 fragment kept activity 2 and normalized the fragment to #activity-2; Previous moved to activity 1. No page errors. DESIGN.md says a disallowed fragment normalizes to the canonical allowed fragment; I read disallowed as a locked or out-of-range #activity-N fragment, which normalizes here, while a non-activity fragment can be a legitimate in-page anchor (headings carry ids) and is left in place without any state change, which matches the reconciled scope (non-activity fragments must preserve the current activity). The accepted defect (foreign fragments keep the current activity; the guard is effective) is resolved. A separate, pre-existing defect in the same fallback (the corrective location.hash assignment pushes a new history entry, which creates a Back loop in the sandbox after a locked fragment) is filed as a new low finding, pyf-sme-loop4-syntax-001; it does not reopen this item.

Loop-4 ruling on current bytes at d3715dcd (HEAD 1a645b15; sha256 e3de63fb53e42e04096263aeb25d9b79688075ecc33da7cd4a4fae551b2610f1). The print rule (line 153) now also shows the hidden recap section (section.pep-act without data-pep-activity), hides its workspace child, and reveals hidden [data-step] nodes inside its reading region. Verified with Playwright 1.55 Chromium from the repository node_modules (no screenshots, no traces) and print media emulated from a fresh activity 1: all 4 activity sections, every task block and every checks block render; the recap section, its Recap heading and all four recap bullets render with every ancestor displayed, after the last activity in source order; the recap workspace (with its completion message) does not render, so no early finished claim prints; topic-bar navigation, Previous, Continue and back links are hidden; unattempted sections print no feedback, verdict, correct/wrong marker or retry question; from activity 2 (after the public activity-1 segment) the same holds and the only feedback rendered in a non-current section is that of the activity the learner already attempted; from the recap itself (after the full public route) every activity section and the recap, including its workspace, render. Not fully fixed: the same rule hides the whole recap workspace, and that workspace holds the recap's static model, a summary table inside the recap step's live-model figure. Printed from any activity, that figure does not render, and 4 of its 6 rows appear nowhere else in the printed text (body innerText under print media after beforeprint). It renders only when printing from the recap itself. So part of the recap's teaching content is still omitted from print before the learner reaches it, which is the accepted defect (DESIGN.md Print: every enrolled page prints non-empty teaching content). Recommendation: in print, show the recap workspace's model figure as well, and keep hiding only the parts that would claim completion early (the ask region with the finished line and the completion message). Open.
